extracted.intended_audience: fiction writers (especially novelists/newer writers) struggling with plot, structure, and revision
extracted.subtask_short: novel plotting with Save The Cat
extracted.subtask_description: Advice on using three-act structure and Blake Snyder's Save The Cat (BS2) beat sheet to plan/revise novels, including an extra recommended beat for stronger endings. Emphasizes internalizing beats without rigid outlining.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-act structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Three act structure: Set-up, Confrontation, Resolution. This is screenwriting shorthand for how to plan out and plot a story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Know the three-act breakdown as a planning/plottng shorthand even if you don't outline rigidly; it helps identify broad story phases and where beats belong.

rubrics_metrics.name: Save The Cat Beat Sheet (BS2) — overall
rubrics_metrics.description: Blake Snyder's SAVE THE CAT boils down storytelling beats in a three act structure to cute, quippy concepts that are easy to digest/latch onto.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use BS2 as a shorthand/critiquing tool: find the Blake Snyder Beat Sheet online and consult breakdowns of popular novels using BS2 to spot missing beats and improve pacing/structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opening Image
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the BS2 beat list — serves as the story's opening snapshot. (Author notes they will discuss specific beats in later chapters.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Theme Stated
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the BS2 beat list — delivers the story's thematic seed early on so later events can echo/answer it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set Up
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the BS2 beat list — establishes characters, world, status quo, and stakes that will be disrupted by the inciting incident.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inciting Incident
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the BS2 beat list — the event that propels the protagonist out of the status quo and launches the main plot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Debate
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the BS2 beat list — the protagonist wrestles with the decision to act; useful for clarifying stakes and internal resistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Break into Two
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the BS2 beat list — transition into Act Two where the protagonist commits to the new direction, shifting the story's energy and challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: B Story
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the BS2 beat list — secondary narrative thread (often relational) that supports theme and character growth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fun and Games / Promise of the Premise
rubrics_metrics.description: Fun and Games or "Promise of the Premise"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the BS2 beat list — the section that delivers on the story's central concept and gives the reader the expected pleasures; often where the premise is explored in scenes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Midpoint
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the BS2 beat list — a turning point that raises the stakes or changes the game's nature; can be a false victory or disaster that shifts momentum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bad Guys Close In
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the BS2 beat list — escalating external and internal pressures that tighten the conflict toward crisis.

rubrics_metrics.name: All Is Lost
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the BS2 beat list — the apparent defeat or lowest point; often paired with a symbolic 'whiff of death' moment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dark Night of the Soul
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the BS2 beat list — the protagonist's internal reckoning before finding the solution or resolve to act in Act Three.

rubrics_metrics.name: Break into Three
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the BS2 beat list — the pivot into Act Three where knowledge/resolve from the Dark Night yields the plan to confront the final conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finale
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the BS2 beat list — the active, often multi-scene resolution where the protagonist executes the final plan and thematic threads are resolved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Image
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the BS2 beat list — the closing snapshot that contrasts with the Opening Image to show change; the last impression left with the reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use BS2 shorthand for critiquing and diagnosing missing beats
rubrics_metrics.description: There are beats that many newer writers miss, and working on them can totally turn their novel around.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the BS2 beat names as diagnostic labels when giving or receiving critique to find which sections of a manuscript lack necessary beats or momentum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absorb beats via reading, watching, and observing
rubrics_metrics.description: Read, watch, observe. I've read so many books, and watched so much television, and so many movies--I have absorbed story beats and structure and storytelling devices by osmosis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If outlining and structure-books frustrate you, internalize beats through broad exposure to fiction and media so beats come naturally in drafting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't follow structure religiously
rubrics_metrics.description: The idea of religiously following story structure sucks all the joy from my heart and doesn't make me want to write.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use structure as a helpful framework rather than a rigid formula; adapt beats to your voice and project so they support creativity instead of stifling it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include 'The Calm After The Storm' beat
rubrics_metrics.description: The Calm After The Storm — Arcs & emotions should firmly resolve here, and you should allow the reader to breathe before The End.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work this beat in after the Finale, before the Final Image (or pair it with the Final Image). Many endings that feel rushed or unsatisfying are missing this moment; use it to resolve emotional arcs and give readers closure.
